Home-cooked meals from your neighbors.

Neighbor Nosh is a simple, free board where people who need regular home-cooked meals post what they're looking for — and neighbors who already love to cook offer to make a few extra portions.

How it works

Three steps, and then it's just you and your neighbor. Neighbor Nosh makes the introduction — everything after that happens directly between the two of you.

1

Post what you need

Put up a short, public post: your first name, your age, your general area, how many meals a week, and any dietary needs. That's it.

Posts never show
  • Your home address
  • Your phone number or email
  • Anything you didn't write yourself
2

Cooks apply to you

Nearby home cooks who'd like to help send you an application. Only you can see applications to your post — they aren't public.

Every application includes
  • The cook's name and where they live
  • A little about themselves
  • Their general pricing per meal
  • Their email and phone, for you only
3

Call or text them directly

Like an application? Call or text the cook yourself and work it out together — menus, price, and delivery or pickup, all between you.

You arrange it your way
  • Pay the cook directly — cash, Venmo, whatever suits you both
  • Delivery or pickup, per match
  • No distance limit — that's your call
the short version

It's a neighborhood bulletin board, not a delivery service. Neighbor Nosh doesn't take orders, handle money, or sit in the middle of your arrangement. It just helps the right two neighbors find each other.

who's it for?

Anyone who needs a home-cooked meal, regularly

We're starting with seniors in the Coachella Valley — but the idea was never just for one group. If cooking has become the hard part of eating well, this is for you.

Starting here first

Seniors

Living at home shouldn't mean choosing between fast food and cooking for one. A neighbor cook a few streets away changes that.

Busy parents

Two jobs, three practices, zero time. A neighbor who already cooks for their own family can add your weeknight dinners to the pot.

College kids

For students eating like students — and the parents who'd sleep better knowing a real dinner shows up a couple of times a week.

People with disabilities

When cooking isn't possible, eating well still should be. Regular meals from someone nearby, arranged on your terms.

Post your need

This is a working preview of the posting form. Fill it in and your post appears at the top of the board above, exactly as neighbors would see it — first name, age, general area, meals, and dietary needs. Nothing is sent anywhere; it's a draft you can try out.

Keep it general: your neighborhood or city area is plenty. You'll share exact details later, privately, with a cook you choose.

already cooking anyway?

For cooks: just make a few extra portions

Most home cooks already make too much. Neighbor Nosh turns the extra into a little income and a real connection — no restaurant, no delivery shift, no new routine.

  • Totally free to join and to apply. No joining fee, no fee per application, no cut of what you earn — now or as the plan stands.
  • You set your own price per meal and negotiate directly with the person who posted. They pay you — cash, Venmo, whatever you both prefer.
  • Your contact details stay private. Your email and phone go only to the person whose post you applied to — never on the public board.
  • Cook what you already cook. Apply to posts that fit your food, your schedule, and your neighborhood.

why we're doing this

Reinventing the American village, one dinner at a time.

Somewhere along the way, we built a world where it's normal to order dinner from an app across town — and strange to ask the person three doors down, who's already cooking. People who can't cook end up dependent on fast food and expensive restaurants, and neighbors stay strangers.

Neighbor Nosh is a small bet that the village can come back: real home cooking, shared between real neighbors, fostering the kind of connection a delivery driver can't drop off. It's free for everyone, because a village shouldn't have a cover charge.

straight talk

Safety, honestly

We'd rather tell you plainly how this works than dress it up. Neighbor Nosh is a classified-ads style board, and that comes with a clear division of responsibility.

We don't vet cooks

Neighbor Nosh doesn't run background checks, inspect kitchens, or certify anyone. Permits and food-safety rules are each cook's own responsibility. What a cook tells you in their application is theirs to stand behind — so ask questions, the way you would with any classified ad.

It's mostly between you two

Once you call or text a cook, the arrangement — food, price, pickup or delivery — belongs to the two of you, like any arrangement between neighbors. Start small, meet in a way that feels comfortable, and build trust over a few meals.

But you're not stuck

If something goes wrong, you can always report a cook to Neighbor Nosh — and a reported cook's email can be blocked from the board. Reporting is simple, and it's always available, even though the day-to-day arrangement is yours.

good questions

Before you ask

Does Neighbor Nosh cost anything?

No. Posting is free, applying is free, and there's no fee when you match. The plan is to keep it free for everyone and support it later with ads, affiliate revenue, and partnerships with other services.

How does the cook get paid?

Directly by you. You and the cook agree on a price per meal and pay each other the way you like — cash, Venmo, and so on. Neighbor Nosh never touches the money.

Who sees my phone number?

Nobody, from your post — posts show only your first name, age, general area, meals, and dietary needs. If you're a cook, your phone and email appear only inside your application, which only the person who posted can see.

Delivery or pickup?

Whichever the two of you agree on, per match. There's no distance limit either — if a cook across town is worth it to you, that's your call.

Where is this launching?

First in the Coachella Valley, starting with seniors — with cooks and meal-seekers joining at the same time, so the board is useful from day one.
